title: Lemon bars
summary: A sharp, silky lemon custard baked over a crisp almond shortbread base, dairy-free as written.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Line a 20 cm (8 in) square pan with parchment, leaving an overhang.
Mix the crust ingredients, press evenly into the pan and bake 12–15 minutes, until golden. Lower the oven to 160 °C (325 °F).
Whisk the eggs, erythritol and allulose until smooth. Whisk in the lemon juice, zest, coconut flour and salt, then leave 5 minutes for the coconut flour to hydrate and whisk again.
Pour over the warm crust and bake 20–25 minutes, until the filling is set at the edges with only a slight wobble in the centre.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 3 hours. Dust with powdered erythritol and cut into 16 squares with a clean, wet knife.
tips: Strain the filling for the smoothest top; coconut flour can leave a few specks.

origin.history: Lemon bars, also called lemon squares, became common in American community cookbooks in the mid-twentieth century. They descend from older English lemon curd and lemon tarts, pressed into a sheet pan with a shortbread base so they could be cut into squares.
